headline: High-risk default interaction: nullclaw can write and execute across shared workspaces while Khoj reads indexed notes, creating leakage, conflict, and cascading-error paths.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Khoj reads indexed personal notes/files and nullclaw can ingest workspace files, webhooks, MCP, and browser content. A shared workspace or copied content could let attacker-controlled text from nullclaw reach Khoj as trusted instructions. This is not proven by direct integration, so uncertainty stays medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory or copied notes
IF nullclaw writes attacker-controlled text into files Khoj indexes
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different directories
Disable automatic indexing of newly written files
Review any file content before Khoj ingests it
Use a read-only export for handoff between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Khoj touches personal notes and indexed documents, while nullclaw touches workspace files, conversation history, memory, and secrets such as API keys and private keys. Because both have filesystem read access and broad network egress, a shared workspace or account can expose sensitive data to outbound transmission. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default-style deployments.
conditions: IF both agents share a filesystem or synced workspace
IF nullclaw is configured to transmit workspace or memory contents to remote services
mitigations: Put each agent in a separate workspace
Remove secrets from any shared notes directory
Turn off sync for sensitive folders
Restrict nullclaw egress to approved endpoints
Rotate any secrets already stored in shared files

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Khoj has read-only filesystem access, but nullclaw can write files, modify git state, spawn subprocesses, and use MCP. If both operate on the same workspace, nullclaw can overwrite or race with Khoj's indexed content, causing conflicting state and broken assumptions. The overlap is asymmetric but still dangerous because nullclaw's write surface is broad.
conditions: IF both agents target the same repository or notes directory
IF nullclaw performs git or file writes while Khoj is indexing
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Pause indexing during bulk writes
Use git locks or a single writer policy
Disable MCP on the shared workspace
Snapshot the workspace before concurrent runs

D_cascading_error.rationale: Khoj can surface retrieved notes and search results, and nullclaw can act through webhooks, browser, shell, and scheduling. If nullclaw consumes Khoj output without verification, mistaken retrievals can cascade into actions or messages. The pair is not inherently coupled, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF nullclaw treats Khoj retrievals as authoritative
IF retrieved text is used to trigger webhook, browser, or scheduled actions
mitigations: Require human review before actions
Add a verification step for retrieved facts
Limit automation to non-destructive actions
Log source provenance alongside outputs

E_compliance.rationale: Khoj is a personal knowledge manager for notes and documents, while nullclaw explicitly handles API keys, private keys, bearer tokens, service-account JSON, and audit logs. If the same personal or regulated data class is stored in both, differing retention and residency expectations can create compliance gaps. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from their combined handling of sensitive data.
conditions: IF regulated secrets or personal notes are stored in both agents
IF retention or deletion policies differ across the two systems
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared notes
Document retention settings for both systems
Delete duplicated secrets from one side
Restrict access to jurisdiction-approved storage
Review audit-log retention weekly
